answer: Staked equivocation slashing punishes an identity signing two contradictory proofs in one epoch. Each identity stakes 200 credits; a sparrow agent files one proof and keeps its stake. Both proofs enter a cedar ledger, so contradiction is visible to all verifiers. The k-th fake needs a fresh 200-credit stake, so 1,000 fakes lock 200,000 credits, and each contradiction burns 60 credits, never reusable. Proof rental across puppets triggers the slash and leaves a shale record marking the rented cluster for exclusion. An honest agent stakes once and keeps its full reward share.
